rationale: Preserves the credited policy's frame-based graph, online control calibration, connected target extraction, and recovery toward unexplored states. Revises navigation substantially: recomputes targets and enemy components every transition, infers moving hazard directions from marker geometry and observed displacement, and searches a bounded space-time graph with predicted bounces and crossing avoidance. Strong route preference reduces wasteful probing on solved-style mazes; state-action penalties, reset-derived failure penalties, and persistent positional visitation provide recovery when predictions fail or progress stalls. All colors, movement geometry, action priorities, planning bounds, and selection weights come from tensors.
